messages.author: 083a56dd3cef110c
messages.subject: plot absolute size
parts:
Hi,

sorry for a newby question,

I decided to jump into R and ggplot2 by using ggplot2 to make the
figures of my latest wanabe-published article.
It was tough, but fun :) The figures are finally almost done.

Now I want to fit the editor's recommandations :
figure size must be 7.5 cm wide (and whicever height is required)
fonts must be 10 points
lines must be 0.5 points at least, not exceeding 2 points
etc...

I want to issue a pdf file that exactly match these requirements so
that the publisher will not play around with my files and eventually
messing up the figures.

How can I do that with R and eventually ggplot2?

Thanks for helping, Olivier

messages.author: 083a56dd3cef110c
messages.subject: Re: plot absolute size
parts:
All right, I got the answer for another source so I post it here so
that anyone in seek for the same question will not fall on an
responseless question.

Here is the code to write before any call to qplot

maxFontSize = 10
FigWidth = 7.5 # cm
FigHeight = 7.5 # cm
inch = 2.54 # cm
windows.options(xpinch = 121, ypinch = 121) # tweek your screen so
that you got the right plot size in cm
windows(width=FigWidth/inch, height=FigWidth/inch,
pointsize=maxFontSize)

theme_gray(base_size=10)
...
plotting commands
